tasks.requirement: Requirement 4 — productId is added to pendingIds before the fetch call using a functional updater
tasks.description: In toggleFavourite (FavouritesContext.tsx), insert `setPendingIds(prev => new Set(prev).add(productId));` after the optimistic setFavouriteIds block and immediately before the try statement. This makes isPending(productId) return true for the duration of the in-flight request, causing FavouriteButton to disable itself.

tasks.requirement: Requirements 2 and 3 — catch block reverts the optimistic change for the affected product only, using a functional updater
tasks.description: In the catch block of toggleFavourite, add a setFavouriteIds call using a functional updater that inverts the optimistic change: if wasAdded is true (product was being added), delete productId from the set; if wasAdded is false (product was being removed), add productId back. Form: `setFavouriteIds(prev => { const next = new Set(prev); if (wasAdded) { next.delete(productId); } else { next.add(productId); } return next; });`. Place this before the existing setError call.

tasks.requirement: Requirement 5 — productId is removed from pendingIds unconditionally in a finally block
tasks.description: After the catch block in toggleFavourite, add a finally block containing `setPendingIds(prev => { const next = new Set(prev); next.delete(productId); return next; });`. This ensures cleanup happens whether the fetch succeeded or failed, with no duplication in try or catch branches.
